factors.name: Size and parallel branching
factors.summary: Measures of net size and of parallel and choice branching load highly together (Number of empty sequence flows 0.95, Size 0.86, Token split 0.82, Connector Mismatch 0.75, Control flow complexity 0.72), so larger nets in this dataset also tend to have more splits and more places between parallel splits and joins. Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factor 2 (0.64), Token split loads moderately on Factor 2 (0.48), and Size loads moderately on Factor 3 (0.45).

factors.name: Connectivity and connector degree
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.88) and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.83) define this factor, which captures how many arcs attach to nodes, especially to the largest connector. Control flow complexity (0.64, cross-loading with Factor 1) and Token split (0.48) contribute secondarily, which fits the shared notion of arcs leaving splits.

factors.name: Sparseness and separability
factors.summary: Density loads negatively (-0.78) and Separability positively (0.61), so the factor contrasts sparse, more separable nets with dense ones; Size also loads moderately here (0.45), consistent with density shrinking as nets grow. Sequentiality is only weakly assigned (-0.35) with similar loadings on all three factors and a low communality (0.32), so it adds little to the interpretation.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett's test significant, overall KMO 0.82), and three varimax-rotated factors explain about 78% of the variance across 288 nets. The dominant factor (40%) combines size with parallel branching measures; the second (23%) captures connectivity, i.e. arcs per node and maximum connector degree; the third (15%) contrasts density with separability. Control flow complexity cross-loads on the first two factors, and Sequentiality is poorly explained by the solution.
caveats: Control flow complexity loads similarly on Factor 1 (0.72) and Factor 2 (0.64) and cannot be cleanly attributed to one factor.
Sequentiality has a low communality (0.32) and near-equal weak loadings on all factors, so its assignment to Factor 3 is uncertain.
Connector Heterogeneity and Average connector degree were removed by the MSA filter and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so these aspects are not represented.
The third eigenvalue (1.06) is barely above 1, so Factor 3 is comparatively weak and depends on the chosen number of factors.
The Bartlett degrees of freedom (66) correspond to 12 measures rather than the 10 used, suggesting the test was computed before MSA filtering.
The factors reflect shared variance among measures in this set of discovered nets, not causal structure, and may differ for other data or rotations.
